gaps.title: A — NDSU Reproduction (Substitute Data)
gaps.problem_statement: The original QuIM-RAG paper (Saha et al. 2024) reports results on a private NDSU catalog/career-advising corpus that is not available to this project. Exact reproduction of those numbers is not possible.
gaps.dataset: OHR-Bench manual+textbook domains (substitute for NDSU catalog/career-advising; NOT the original private corpus)
gaps.proposed: QuIM-style question-indexed retrieval vs. this project's Hybrid/EAR pipeline
gaps.uncertainty: No significance test run between Traditional RAG and QuIM-style on this substitute dataset (single run, not bootstrapped) -- a gap in this analysis, stated not hidden.
gaps.limitations: This is a SUBSTITUTE-DATA study, not a reproduction of Saha et al. 2024's published numbers. Embedding model (MiniLM vs. their bge-large-en-v1.5), question generation (heuristic template vs. their GPT-3.5), and dataset (OHR-Bench manual/textbook vs. their private NDSU catalog/career-advising corpus) all differ -- see research/NDSU_REPRODUCTION_REPORT.md for the full deviation log. Results here are internally comparable (same dataset/protocol across methods) but NOT comparable to the paper's Table 2 numbers in research/PAPER_REVIEW.md. [2026-10-21 audit note: this gap's EAR-gating result depends on the same un-corrected calibration/evaluation split family that final_validation_ear_core_claim found to be document-overlapping; this gap's own split was NOT independently checked for the same issue, so its EAR-dependent numbers should be treated as unverified, not confirmed, until re-checked. See research/FINAL_VALIDATION/CLAIM_VERIFICATION_MATRIX.md.]

gaps.title: B — OCR Robustness & EAR Validation
gaps.problem_statement: EAR's ocr_confidence signal was calibrated only on OHR-Bench's clean ground-truth text (zero OCR noise variance), so its real-world value for retrieval decisions was unvalidated.
gaps.dataset: 15 OHR-Bench documents, text rendered then synthetically degraded at 3 severities + clean baseline (4 conditions)
gaps.proposed: Degraded-document retrieval with vs. without the ocr_confidence signal
gaps.uncertainty: Pearson correlation p=1.403e-30 (n=41); small sample, see report for caveats.
gaps.limitations: Degradation is SYNTHETIC image corruption of real text, not genuine scanner noise. Small sample (~18 documents) relative to the full OHR-Bench corpus, and restricted to pages whose ground truth is prose-renderable (table/formula-markup pages were excluded -- rendering literal LaTeX table syntax onto a page and OCR'ing it is not a meaningful OCR-noise simulation, an issue found and fixed during this run; see the report). Retrieval engines here index one page per document (not full multi-page documents) to isolate the OCR-condition effect.

gaps.title: C — End-to-End Generation Quality
gaps.problem_statement: All prior evaluation in this project was retrieval-only. No metric has ever been computed on an answer this project actually generated.
gaps.dataset: OHR-Bench evaluation split, stratified 60-query sample (10/domain, seed 23)
gaps.proposed: Local LLM answer, generated only when EAR does not abstain
gaps.uncertainty: Single run, no bootstrap CI on the RAGAS/generation metrics in this pass (60-query sample) -- a gap, stated not hidden.
gaps.limitations: RAGAS metrics are this project's own implementation (quimrag/ragas_eval.py) of the published definitions, judged by a LOCAL llama3.2:latest (3.2B) model via Ollama -- not the `ragas` PyPI package, and not validated against a cloud-scale judge (GPT-4/Claude) the way the original RAGAS metric family was. A smaller local model (llama3.2:1b) was tested and found unreliable for claim-extraction tasks even at temperature=0 (see module docstring) -- documented, and worked around with a two-step extract-then-verify prompt design, not silently accepted. No API key was needed since generation and judging both run locally via Ollama. [2026-10-21 audit note: this gap's EAR-gating result depends on the same un-corrected calibration/evaluation split family that final_validation_ear_core_claim found to be document-overlapping; this gap's own split was NOT independently checked for the same issue, so its EAR-dependent numbers should be treated as unverified, not confirmed, until re-checked. See research/FINAL_VALIDATION/CLAIM_VERIFICATION_MATRIX.md.]

gaps.title: D — RVQ Recall Gap Analysis
gaps.problem_statement: The project's 2-stage RVQ compresses embeddings 341x-768x but loses substantial Recall@5 (e.g. 0.378 exact -> 0.161-0.283 quantized) versus exact dense search, with the root cause not yet diagnosed.
gaps.dataset: OHR-Bench evaluation split (same 252-query set as research/BASELINE_COMPARISON.md)
gaps.proposed: RVQ with candidate fix (exact-rerank of quantized top-N)
gaps.uncertainty: Welch's t-test on reconstruction cosine, lost vs. not-lost gold chunks: p=3.54e-06
gaps.limitations: Root-cause isolated to quantization reconstruction error specifically (dense-only comparison, no hybrid fusion/rerank/threshold confound). Candidate fix requires keeping exact vectors for the candidate pool, which is itself a storage/latency tradeoff, not a free fix -- see report.

gaps.title: FINAL VALIDATION — EAR Core Claim Re-Checked Under Document-Disjoint Split
gaps.problem_statement: A 2026-10-21 research-grade audit found the calibration/evaluation split used for every prior EAR selective-prediction measurement (ndsu_reproduction aside) was document-overlapping: 52/102 (51%) calibration documents also appeared in evaluation. This gap re-measures the core EAR claim on a corrected, verified-zero-overlap, document-disjoint split.
gaps.dataset: OHR-Bench qas_v2.json (corrected from qas.json), document-level-disjoint split (corrected from row-level)
gaps.proposed: EAR-gated selective accuracy on the document-disjoint split
gaps.uncertainty: 95% CI on the corrected improvement includes zero -- the core EAR selective-prediction claim is NOT statistically significant under the corrected split, superseding the original (leaky-split) CI which excluded zero.
gaps.limitations: This gap re-ran only the main benchmark (baseline comparison + EAR fit/eval). It did NOT re-run the ndsu_reproduction or generation_quality gaps below, which still use the uncorrected split family and are flagged as unverified-under-correction, not confirmed, in research/FINAL_VALIDATION/CLAIM_VERIFICATION_MATRIX.md.
